chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not get cupping done on Friday during the midday sun (Zawal), for whoever gets cupping done at that time on Friday and something happens to him, let him not blame anyone but himself.

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Midday sun; the time when the sun reaches its zenith and begins to decline, often associated with noon prayers or specific times of day.
key_terms.فَأَصَابَهُ شَيْءٌ: If something happens to him; referring to any harm, illness, or adverse effect resulting from the action.
key_terms.لَا يَلُومَنَّ إِلَّا نَفْسَهُ: He should not blame anyone but himself; indicating personal responsibility for the outcome.
key_terms.يَحْتَجِمُوا: To get cupping done; plural imperative form of the ritual practice of hijama.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on getting cupping done on Friday noon in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi advises against performing cupping (hijama) on Friday during Zawal (midday), linking the practice to potential physical weakness or harm. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted through the lens of *takhassus* (specific precaution) or *khasf* (divine concealment of merit), suggesting that while not strictly forbidden, the timing carries a higher risk of adverse effects, placing the burden of care on the individual. The warning serves as a practical medical and spiritual guideline for maintaining vitality during the holy day of Jumu'ah.
